summary: Mars Safe Path is an interactive web-based educational prototype developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, focusing on the Jezero Crater region of Mars. It combines three NASA Mars Trek imagery layers—Viking visible imagery, MGS MOLA colour hillshade and THEMIS daytime infrared imagery—using HTML, CSS, JavaScript and Leaflet.js. Users can explore different map layers, select starting and destination points, and compare a direct route with an A* pathfinding algorithm that identifies a lower-cost path using a synthetic 16 × 16 traversal-cost grid. The project addresses the challenge by demonstrating how planetary imagery and intelligent route-planning techniques can support Martian surface exploration. It is important because future Mars exploration requires careful terrain assessment and efficient route planning for robotic and human missions. This prototype provides an educational foundation for developing advanced Mars navigation systems using real terrain and hazard data.
details: Mars Safe Path is an interactive educational web application designed to demonstrate how planetary mapping and intelligent route-planning techniques can support future Mars exploration. Focused on the Jezero Crater region, the application allows users to explore three independently selectable NASA Mars Trek imagery layers: Viking visible imagery, MGS MOLA colour hillshade and Mars Odyssey THEMIS daytime infrared imagery. Users can select starting and destination points, generate routes using the A* pathfinding algorithm, and compare the suggested route with a direct path using approximate distance and traversal-cost metrics. The project helps users understand how different remote-sensing datasets provide complementary views of the Martian surface and how algorithms can balance distance with modelled traversal costs. Its intended impact is to improve awareness of planetary mapping, terrain exploration and computational route planning while inspiring interest in space science and technology. The application was developed using HTML, CSS, JavaScript and Leaflet.js, with NASA Mars Trek WMTS imagery and an A* algorithm operating on a synthetic 16 × 16 cost grid. Its creative aspect lies in combining multiple NASA imagery layers with an interactive route-planning demonstration in a single user-friendly platform. We considered map accessibility, ease of interaction, different visual perspectives of Mars, route comparison and scientific transparency. The current prototype is educational; its synthetic costs are not actual terrain measurements or detected hazards. Future development could integrate real elevation and terrain data to improve route-planning accuracy.
